title: Audit-append **concurrency contention.** `SqlAuditSink` takes no application-level lock: two genuinely concurrent state-changing requests both read the same chain tip (`TipHashAsync`) and race the `audit.AuditEvents` `PreviousHash` UNIQUE index — the loser gets SQL error 2601 (duplicate key) and the whole operation **500s** (fail-closed, but a hard error rather than a retry). Accepted at design time (ADR-0009/0026 + the `SqlAuditSink.cs` `ponytail:` note — "negligible at ≤20-user on-prem scale; if it ever bites, serialize via `sp_getapplock` or retry"). **Reproduced 2026-07-13** by the P15b live VR: the SPA's login-time `Membership.ProfileSynced` append raced an immediate seed burst, so one `Research.MissionProposed` lost the race and 500'd (audit seq 12/13 both chained off tip `1f738021`). Fix (the pre-named upgrade path): a **bounded retry** on 2601/2627 inside `AppendAsync` — re-read tip, recompute hash, re-insert — which preserves chain linearity + the fail-closed guarantee; or `sp_getapplock` serialization. **2026-07-13 — operator chose to fix now**, then (after adversarial review) to fix it **robustly** rather than cheaply. Arc: a first pass added a bounded optimistic-retry in `SqlAuditSink`; CI then showed the 8-way stress case **deadlocks (SQL 1205)**, whose victim's transaction is rolled back → in-place retry cannot recover. A devil's-advocate review further found a **sink-level app lock is lock-order-unsafe** (handlers like `IssueDecision`/`VerifyAction` emit-then-write-more, inverting `{lock, module-rows}` order). **✅ RESOLVED 2026-07-13 via ADR-0028 (serialize at tx-open):** `AmbientTransaction.EnsureStartedAsync` takes a **transaction-scoped exclusive `sp_getapplock`** ('acmp-audit-chain') immediately after `BeginTransaction` — before any module write — so every audited write-command acquires the chain lock first (one consistent order → no cross-handler deadlock) and appends serialize (no fork, no 1205). Held to commit ⇒ next command reads a committed tip; `THROW` on lock-timeout ⇒ fail-closed; SQL-Server-only (degrades to no-op elsewhere). The **denial/autocommit path** (no ambient tx) keeps the bounded retry as its backstop (broadened to catch the `PreviousHash` **or** `Hash` index race; deadlock-free — no crosswise module locks). Tests: `Concurrent_commands_all_commit_without_forking_the_audit_chain` (8 write-commands serialize) + `Concurrent_denials_all_record_their_audit_via_the_retry_without_forking_the_chain` (8 denials converge via retry) + the same-tx atomicity suite, all green (CI-proven for the write-command deadlock case). No schema/migration.

title: **Inline `style={{}}` usage in the SPA — style hygiene, NOT a security control.** ~110 inline-style sites across ~25 components (18 static, 7 dynamic + `SortableList.tsx`'s @dnd-kit drag transform). title: ADR-0038 DEPLOY PLUMBING (§5) — DONE 2026-08-12 (PR #237, main 122f41d). What shipped, and how it differs from the plan this row was raised with: THE CLIENT IS DEFINED IN reconcile.sh, NOT IN realm-export.json (DEF-049). Keycloak imports the bundled export only on FIRST run, so a client declared there reaches a fresh stack and never appears on prod or UAT — the DEF-023 / CHANGE-004 seam a third time. The client SECRET settled it: a secret can only be made to match gen-secrets' file by being SET from that file, so the client cannot be expressed in the export at all. reconcile.sh now creates-or-updates the client, re-asserts confidential + service-account-only on every run, sets the secret FROM the mounted file, and RECONCILES THE GRANT AS AN EXACT SET — revoking anything outside it, so a widened grant cannot survive a deploy — then reads the result back rather than trusting exit codes. THE GRANT IS `manage-users` AND NOTHING ELSE (OQ-070), and it now has a gate: check-realm-export.mjs asserts the EXACT set with realm-admin named forbidden, and BOTH failure branches were proven by forcing them (adding view-realm; granting realm-admin). The grant lives in deploy/keycloak/admin-client.env so the gate and the reconciler read the SAME value — a check reading a different file passes while the deployment drifts — and it needed a .gitignore exception, because `*.env` would have silently excluded the one file both of them depend on (the gate passed locally only because the file existed on disk). ENABLING IS ONE VARIABLE, which removes the boot-stopping sequencing hazard this row was raised warning about: the secret is ALWAYS written, unlike the Webex block, because a compose secrets: entry whose file is missing fails the whole stack, and because ValidateOnStart means a flag arriving before its secret STOPS api and worker rather than degrading. 09-put-env.sh now refuses that exact combination at the last point before it reaches a machine; gen-secrets GENERATES a value when unset rather than failing, so an operator .env predating the variable still boots — with no literal fallback, because a default credential in a script is a credential. The worker got identical config: it composes the same Membership module, so a flag without a secret would fail ITS validator too. VERIFIED SAFE FOR THE LIVE BOX BEFORE MERGING: 08-bootstrap-box.sh:164 runs gen-secrets BEFORE compose up at :207, so the new secret file always exists on a real deploy. ⚠ WHAT IS NOT YET EVIDENCED, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: that the reconciler actually CREATED the client anywhere. CI's e2e boots the full stack against a real Keycloak and passed, but DEF-051 records that nothing depends on keycloak-config — so a failed reconcile leaves the stack healthy, and A GREEN E2E IS NOT EVIDENCE THE CLIENT EXISTS. Closing that assertion is DEF-051's job; the AC-090 behavioural leg additionally needs a deploy with KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ENABLED=true.

title: GUEST ACCESS WINDOWS FOLLOW THE MEETING - DONE 2026-08-12 (PR #244, main 5afe40f), and the row's own premise turned out to be FALSE. As raised this row said 'rescheduling a meeting does not move a guest's already-written window'. ACMP HAS NO RESCHEDULE: Meeting.ScheduledStart/End are private-set and assigned only in the Schedule factory, there is no PUT/PATCH on /api/meetings, and no feature mutates them - three independent checks. A meeting is scheduled once, then started, held or cancelled. So nothing was built for reschedule; IGuestWindowWriter takes an arbitrary instant precisely so a future reschedule can call it with the new end plus GuestAccess.Grace. WHAT DID SHIP is what DEC-041 added when it widened the scope, and those are the EXPOSURE cases rather than the inconvenience one: cancelling a meeting CLOSES its guest presenters' windows (an outsider must not keep live read access to material for a meeting that will not happen); removing the agenda item CLOSES it (the slot the access was granted for is gone); reassigning the slot CLOSES the replaced guest's window, while re-assigning the SAME person is a no-op. DESIGN NOTE WORTH KEEPING: IGuestWindowWriter is a SEPARATE port from IGuestProvisioner for availability, not tidiness - the provisioner is registered only when the Keycloak admin client is configured, so folding this in would have made CANCELLING A MEETING FAIL wherever in-app user management is off, which is every environment today. This port creates nothing (one nullable column) so it is registered unconditionally, like IPrincipalRevalidator. TWO SAFETY PROPERTIES, both proven by tests rather than argued: a guest holding a SECOND slot keeps their access (the rule is 'close it only if they no longer present any slot on a live meeting', checked against the store after the change, not reasoned about); and an ORDINARY member never acquires an expiry, because the port only touches rows that already hold a window - a member handed one by accident would be locked out of the whole product and DEF-029 means the row could never be deleted to recover.
activation_trigger: Reschedule: if a reschedule feature is ever built, it must call IGuestWindowWriter with the new ScheduledEnd + GuestAccess.Grace. Nothing else outstanding.

title: Stream.IsWildcard SHIPS WITH NO PRODUCTION READER, DELIBERATELY - and that is DW-026's exact signature, so it is registered here rather than left to be re-discovered as a fifth instance. WHAT LANDED (ADR-0042 step 1, PR 'feat/def-057-step1-seed-streams'): a bool column on membership.streams, a filtered unique index enforcing at most one wildcard row, and a seed of the committee's five delivery streams plus the wildcard. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST YET: any code that READS the column. Grep IsWildcard after this PR and you get the entity property, the EF configuration, the migration and the integration tests - and no production consumer. That is precisely how Topic.Reopen, Stream.Create, StreamScopeRequirement and Topic.SetScope each presented, so a reviewer applying DW-026's own lesson SHOULD flag this. This row is the answer to that flag. WHY IT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT, and the reasoning is ADR-0042's ordering, which the ADR calls load-bearing and non-negotiable: the reader is the authorization path, and wiring the authorization path before every member has been assigned a stream locks the entire committee out (all 26 production members were seeded straight into Keycloak, so the invite-time stream field does not cover them - ADR-0042 consequence (1), the one marked CERTAIN). The column must therefore EXIST, and be seeded, several PRs before anything consults it. Landing them together is the failure mode the ADR explicitly warns about: 'anyone treating it as one change will land the seed without the parts that make it safe'. THE NAMED FUTURE READER, so this is not an open-ended promise: UserStreamProvider (Membership.Infrastructure/Authorization/MembershipAbacProviders.cs), consumed by StreamScopeHandler, at ADR-0042 STEP 7. ⚠ THE READER CANNOT BE ADDED WITHOUT A PORT CHANGE, which is the real reason it is not a one-line follow-up: IUserStreamProvider.GetAssignedStreamsAsync returns IReadOnlyCollection<string> - a bare list of stream CODES. Wildcard-ness cannot travel through that return type without matching on the wildcard's code, which is EXACTLY what ADR-0042 clause (3) forbids (a magic string in an authorization control breaks silently on rename or re-code, or hands universal access to a future stream that collides with it). So step 7 must widen the port to carry the assigned codes AND a HasWildcard flag - symmetric with the AffectsAllStreams primitive bool that ADR-0042 clause (6) already mandates on IStreamScopedResource for the same cross-module reason (ADR-0001: the contract lives in Acmp.Shared.Contracts, the enum in Topics.Domain; ADR-0021 is the pattern). ⚠ UNTIL STEP 7 LANDS, ASSIGNING THE WILDCARD STREAM TO A MEMBER GRANTS NOTHING AND REFUSES NOTHING - it is inert data. It is not a latent bypass: no code path consults it, so it cannot widen access. The genuine risk in the interval is the opposite one - an administrator assigning 'All streams' through the (still to be built) UI and reasonably believing it took effect. That is why the assignment UI is step 3 and the wiring is step 7, with the backfill at step 5 in between. INVARIANT AT STAKE: same as DW-026 - a control that is never evaluated is indistinguishable from an implemented one. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-15 (DEC-048 d1): THE TRIGGER FIRED AND THE PREMISE IS NO LONGER TRUE. The column now has THREE production readers - UserStreamProvider reads it and returns IsUnrestricted from ONE query (a flag from a column, never a code match, exactly as ADR-0042 clause (3) required), StreamScopeRequirement consumes that verdict, and the DEC-046 reconciliation grants that stream to every member row it creates. The port widening this row predicted as the blocker is what step 7 actually did. ⚠ What is NOT claimed by closing this: the wildcard path has not yet run in PRODUCTION - that is DEF-065's deploy step and is tracked there, not here.
activation_trigger: ADR-0042 step 7 (wiring StreamScopeRequirement into the stream-bounded write policies). title: EVIDENCE THE 162 REQUIREMENTS THAT HAVE NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — the real remediation behind DEF-012, separated from it because it is a programme rather than a defect fix. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DEFINES THE WORK, taken 2026-08-16: this package holds 222 requirements; EXACTLY 60 have at least one active acceptance criterion and EXACTLY those 60 are Implemented; EXACTLY 162 have NO acceptance criterion and EXACTLY those 162 are Approved. The correlation is perfect, and it is mechanical rather than coincidental: a requirement advances to Implemented ONLY through the auto-advance trigger, which fires when every non-retired AC of that requirement has a latest verdict of Met, so a requirement with no ACs can never advance no matter how thoroughly it shipped. CONSEQUENCE: requirement status in this package is a proxy for 'did anyone write an acceptance criterion', not for 'was this built'. Everything downstream inherits that — v_backlog lists all 155 wbs_items as open (DEF-012), and any reader treating requirement status as a completion signal is reading a coverage statistic instead. INVARIANT AT STAKE, stated here because the column is a foreign key and no invariant row covers it: the package is the record, and a status that reflects whether anyone WROTE an acceptance criterion rather than whether the thing was BUILT makes every downstream view a coverage statistic wearing the costume of a completion signal. WHAT THE WORK IS: for each of the 162, either write an acceptance criterion and audit it with evidence, or record explicitly that the requirement is not separately verifiable and why. ⚠ IT MUST NOT BE DONE BY BULK-ADVANCING REQUIREMENT STATUS — that is the manufactured-status failure DEF-010 records, and DEF-012's own row already refuses the equivalent shortcut for work items. ⚠ AND IT MUST NOT BE DONE BY THE MECHANICAL SHORTCUT THAT LOOKS SOUND: 'close a work item when every requirement it names is Implemented' was tried and is UNSOUND — it closes WBS-20.4, the email adapter, on the strength of the Implemented FR-130, while 'no email in v1, in-app centre only' is a hard constraint of this project (DEC-055). title: NFR-035's 'NO HARDCODED DISPLAY STRINGS' CLAUSE HAS NO CONTROL, while its other clause is well guarded. THE 'NO HARDCODED STRINGS' HALF IS NOT GUARDED AT ALL. check-i18n compares the two resource files against each other; it cannot see a component. Nothing else fills the gap: .oxlintrc.json carries no rule against literal JSX text, and there is no equivalent check anywhere in scripts/ or the workflows. So a developer who types a label directly into a component ships an untranslatable string that the i18n gate is structurally incapable of noticing - the EN/AR files stay in perfect parity because the string never entered them. title: NFR-012 (audit log sustains >= 100 append-only writes/second for 60 s without data loss or lock contention) IS NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THIS REPOSITORY, and it is the performance row most worth eventually measuring. AuditAtomicityTests already proves concurrent commands do not FORK the chain, which is the correctness question; the throughput question is separate and unmeasured. title: NFR-053 vs ADR-0037: THE SPA'S BUILD-TIME OIDC CONFIG IS A RATIFIED TRADE-OFF, NOT AN OVERSIGHT - AND NOBODY RECORDED THAT IT PUTS A MUST REQUIREMENT IN DIVERGENCE. ⚠ THIS ROW WAS FIRST WRITTEN WITH THE WRONG FRAMING (DW-029 batch 13) and is corrected here. THE MECHANICAL FACTS ARE UNCHANGED AND ALL VERIFIED: deploy/Dockerfile.web declares VITE_OIDC_AUTHORITY / VITE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID / VITE_OIDC_SCOPE as build ARGs consumed by npm run build; src/Acmp.Web/src/auth/authConfig.ts reads them through import.meta.env, which Vite resolves at BUILD time; so moving the web image between environments requires a rebuild. The backend is fully env-overridable and the nginx CSP origins are templated at container start via envsubst, so two of the three deployment surfaces do satisfy NFR-053. WHAT THE ORIGINAL ROW GOT WRONG: it read as though nobody had noticed. Two Approved rows say otherwise, and the row named neither. ADR-0037 (ratified 2026-07-24) DECIDES it - 'VITE_OIDC_AUTHORITY is a build arg so the web image is per-environment (web:<sha>-uat / -prod)' - and accepts the cost in its own consequences: 'two web images per commit (runtime OIDC-config injection would collapse them - deferred, OQ-061)'. OQ-061 is Approved and resolved: 'DECIDED 2026-07-24: defer. Two build-tagged images are the smaller step now; runtime injection is a source change to revisit later.' CI implements the decision faithfully, pushing web:<sha>-uat and web:<sha>-prod per commit. THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS A REAL ONE: ADR-0037 accepted a build/deploy consequence, and neither it nor OQ-061 records that the same consequence puts NFR-053 - a MUST-priority requirement whose text forbids image rebuilds for an environment switch - in permanent divergence. A decision may absolutely override a requirement; what is missing is the row saying it did. So this is a requirement-versus-decision reconciliation for the OPERATOR, not engineering work an agent should pick up. THE THREE ROUTES, all operator-only: (a) supersede ADR-0037's build-arg clause with a new ADR and re-open OQ-061, then build runtime injection - the nginx template already envsubsts at container start and is the pattern to copy; (b) keep ADR-0037 and narrow NFR-053 by scope change so its text matches the ratified decision; (c) keep both and record the divergence deliberately, which is the cheapest and leaves the register honest. ⚠ DO NOT BUILD (a) WITHOUT A NEW ADR - ADR rows are FINAL and are superseded, never worked around.
activation_trigger: Operator reconciliation, not an engineering trigger - this row is waiting on a decision rather than on capacity, so it should be closed by a decision row and not by code. It becomes urgent only if the two-image model itself starts costing something real: a UAT-tested web image that cannot be promoted to production by digest the way ADR-0037 promotes the api, worker and sqlserver images, or a third environment making per-environment builds a maintenance burden rather than a one-line CI duplication.

title: MIGRATE THE api AND worker IMAGES TO AN ALPINE OR DISTROLESS BASE - NFR-054's minimal-base clause, KEPT rather than relaxed. THE OPERATOR REJECTED THE RELAXATION, and that is why this row exists. SC-024 was first proposed narrowing BOTH of NFR-054's clauses: the 500 MB cap AND the minimal-base clause, the latter restated as merely 'runtime-only', which would have made Debian-based aspnet:8.0 compliant and closed the finding with no work. The operator declined and approved the SIZE cap narrowing ONLY, keeping 'a minimal base image (e.g. aspnet:8.0-alpine or equivalent distroless)' verbatim. So the divergence becomes TRACKED WORK instead of a relaxed requirement - which is the honest disposition and the harder one. THE FACTS, measured 2026-08-20 (DEF-096): deploy/Dockerfile.backend builds BOTH the api and worker targets FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0, which is Debian-based and neither alpine nor distroless. They pass the size cap comfortably at 257 MB and 245 MB, so this is NOT a size problem - it is an attack-surface one. web already complies (nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.31-alpine, 51 MB). The database image is out of scope entirely under the narrowed text. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COMPLIANCE: alpine and distroless carry materially fewer OS packages and therefore materially fewer CVEs. This repo's trivy-image scan is REPORT-ONLY precisely because base-OS CVEs are unfixable except by a base bump - so a smaller base is the only lever that scan's findings actually respond to. SIZING AND THE REAL RISK: the Dockerfile change is two FROM lines and is trivial. THE RISK IS NOT THE EDIT. Alpine is musl rather than glibc, and this application talks to SQL Server through Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and does culture-aware work in Arabic and English - globalization and native interop are exactly where musl breaks, and ICU behaviour differs. Distroless avoids musl but has no shell, which changes the healthcheck and any entrypoint that shells out; deploy/Dockerfile.backend's worker target and the compose healthchecks would both need review. ⚠ THIS MUST GO THROUGH THE FULL e2e LEG, not just a green unit suite - the failure mode is a runtime globalization or native-load error that compiles and unit-tests perfectly. Verify Arabic search (FREETEXT, LCID 1025) end to end before believing it. ▸▸ DONE 2026-08-29, EXACTLY AS DEC-074 d2 REQUIRED - IN THE SAME CHANGE AS THE FROM-line edit, never separately. The api and worker moved to mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra as DW-080 phase B (PR #325 -> 1d7cb04b, WBS-25.1, DEC-090 d1), so the expensive part - the full e2e leg with Arabic FREETEXT end to end - was spent once rather than twice. ⚠ THE ROW'S RECORDED 257 MB IS STALE BY A RUNTIME MAJOR: it was measured on .NET 8, and .NET 10 made the Debian baseline 326 MB. The achieved figure is 258 MB on chiseled-extra. ⚠ alpine WAS EVALUATED AND NOT CHOSEN, and the reason is not musl: alpine-extra ships ICU 78.1 against chiseled-extra's 74.2, and CLDR moved ar-SA's default calendar between those versions, so the same binary renders a Hijri date on one and a Gregorian one on the other - no exception, no log line, Arabic only.

No N-1 version is pinned for any browser either; Playwright resolves whatever its bundled or channel version is at run time, so even the covered cells prove N, never N/N-1. title: NFR-039'S 'SINGLE SOURCE OF CANONICAL BILINGUAL TERMS' DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE TWO DOCUMENTS THAT CLAIM TO BE IT POINT AT EACH OTHER. NFR-039 (Must, Approved) reads: 'The EN-AR terminology glossary (README section G, localized in design handoff) shall be the single source of canonical bilingual terms; no term shall have more than one AR translation within the application. Target: 0 terminology inconsistencies detected in the i18n resource files.' CLAUSE ONE IS UNMET AND THIS IS PROVABLE WITHOUT READING ANY ARABIC. README.md section G (line 167) is a single paragraph listing 22 English committee terms and its own heading says 'EN-AR pairing finalized in design handoff'. It contains ZERO Arabic characters - measured, with a control proving the detector works, since the same pattern finds 1889 Arabic lines in ar.json. The design handoff (design-handoff/claude-design-input-package.md line 113) says: 'Consistent EN-AR terminology (a shared glossary - see /docs/README section G)'. SO EACH DOCUMENT NAMES THE OTHER AS THE SOURCE AND NEITHER CONTAINS A SINGLE ARABIC TERM. The third candidate, DOC-049 at docs/governance/glossary.md, is EN-only too and states outright in its own preamble that 'EN-AR term pairing is maintained in the design and i18n resources, not in this file' - and it lives under docs/, the frozen read-only archive superseded 2026-07-22. The canonical Arabic that DOES exist is scattered: DEC-032 (Approved) fixes the term family for 'Architecture' as الهيكلة, and everything else lives only in ar.json, which is the artifact the requirement wants CHECKED AGAINST the glossary and therefore cannot also be the glossary. CLAUSE TWO WAS MEASURED AND IS NOT ADJUDICABLE BY A READER OF CODE, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT THING FROM UNMEASURED. Pairing all 1901 keys and grouping short labels of four words or fewer gives 1037 distinct English labels, of which 76 carry more than one Arabic rendering. THAT 76 IS NOT A DEFECT COUNT AND MUST NOT BE REPORTED AS ONE. Arabic adjectives agree in gender with the noun they describe, so 'Accepted' is مقبول describing a risk and مقبولة describing a recommendation, and BOTH ARE CORRECT - collapsing them would be the bug, not the fix. DEC-032 makes the same point about definiteness, recording that dropping ال inside a genitive construct is a grammar RULE rather than a string substitution. Classifying the 76 by whether the renderings share an Arabic stem: 55 are morphological (gender, definiteness, plural) and presumed correct, and 21 are lexically distinct - one concept rendered with genuinely different words. title: NFR-031'S KEYBOARD CLAUSE HAS NO INSTRUMENT, BECAUSE axe IS STATIC ANALYSIS AND CANNOT PRESS A KEY. NFR-031 (Must, Approved) requires all interactive elements - buttons, links, form fields, drag-and-drop handles - to be keyboard accessible, with a keyboard-accessible alternative for drag-and-drop, and targets '100% of interactive elements reachable and operable via keyboard'. WHAT IS GENUINELY BUILT AND WAS VERIFIED: the drag-and-drop alternative EXISTS. AC-043's move up and move down reorder controls are real buttons in the backlog kanban, they are scanned by the live axe pass, and that pass runs with the wcag22aa tag set so target-size (SC 2.5.8, minimum 24 by 24 px) is enforced on them - the e2e spec's own comment says the kanban case was added precisely because that is where target-size bites. WHY THAT IS NOT THE REQUIREMENT: the clause it satisfies is the SECOND one. The first - 100 percent of interactive elements reachable and OPERABLE via keyboard - is not tested anywhere, and cannot be tested by the instrument in place. axe-core is a STATIC analysis of the rendered DOM: it can see that an element has a role, an accessible name and a sufficient hit area, and it flags positive tabindex and some focus-order hazards, but it does not press Tab, does not follow focus, and cannot tell reachable from unreachable. Neither the jsdom axe test nor the live Playwright axe sweep issues a single keypress. So the coverage that exists is real and is about a different property. WHY A DEFERRED-WORK ROW: one clause verified and the headline clause uninstrumented is a partial, and an AC could only record Partial - which, because acs-met counts by retired_in and ignores lifecycle_status, would hold package readiness false permanently. DO NOT LET A LATER SESSION ADD THE MISSING CRITERION; the gap is a missing test, not a missing record.
activation_trigger: Whenever a keyboard-driven walkthrough is next run, or the first time a keyboard-only user reports being unable to reach a control. Also fires if any new drag-and-drop affordance ships, since the requirement's keyboard-alternative clause applies to each one and only the backlog reorder currently has one. CHEAPEST FIRST STEP: a Playwright spec that tabs through one authenticated screen and asserts every focusable element receives a visible focus ring and that no interactive element is skipped - Playwright can drive real Tab keypresses, which is the capability axe structurally lacks.

title: NFR-032'S TARGET NAMES AN axe-core SCAN AND ONE EXISTS, BUT IT COVERS THREE ROUTES OF FIFTY-TWO. NFR-032 (Must, Approved) requires all non-decorative images, icons and data visualizations to carry alternative text or ARIA labels in both EN and AR, and targets '0 non-decorative images without alt text per axe-core scan'. THE INSTRUMENT THE TARGET NAMES IS REAL AND IS BETTER THAN ITS REPUTATION: axe-core is already a dependency, and it runs in two places. In jsdom, src/Acmp.Web/src/test/a11y.test.tsx sweeps 5 component surfaces on every change. Live under Playwright, src/Acmp.Web/e2e/rtl-a11y.spec.ts sweeps Backlog, Submit-Topic and the Backlog kanban in BOTH locales with the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa tag sets - so image-alt, svg-img-alt, role-img-alt, button-name and link-name, the rules that decide this requirement, all run against the real rendered app in Arabic as well as English. Every one passes. THE GAP IS COVERAGE, NOT CAPABILITY, and it is the whole finding. The application has 52 routes. The live sweep visits three of them. A requirement whose target is a scan is satisfied only over what the scan visited, and 'zero violations on three screens' is a true statement that does not answer 'all non-decorative images'. This is the denominator problem in its most literal form: the numerator is genuinely zero and the denominator is six percent. WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY TOO: the three screens chosen are not arbitrary. Backlog is the densest data surface, Submit-Topic is the largest form, and the kanban case was added specifically because the AC-043 reorder controls and drag handles are where target-size bites - the spec says so in its own comment. So the sample is deliberately adversarial rather than convenient, which raises the value of its zero without changing the denominator. title: NFR-033 IS VERIFIED ON ONE OF ITS TWO THRESHOLDS AND ON NONE OF THE FOUR STATES IT NAMES. NFR-033 (Must, Approved) requires colour contrast for all text on background AND FOR UI COMPONENT STATES - normal, hover, focused, disabled - to meet WCAG 2.2 AA, and states two thresholds explicitly: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI components. WHAT EXISTS IS BETTER THAN MOST GATES IN THIS REPOSITORY AND SHOULD NOT BE UNDERSOLD. src/Acmp.Web/src/styles/contrast.test.ts parses tokens.css directly, computes real WCAG relative luminance and contrast ratios, and asserts 20 foreground-on-background token pairs in BOTH the light and the explicit dark palettes - plus a third assertion that the OS-default dark palette inside the prefers-color-scheme media query is IDENTICAL to the explicit one, because they are two hand-maintained copies and only one was reachable by the checks. It also carries its own anti-vacuity guard: before comparing the two dark palettes it asserts the parsed block contains more than ten tokens, so a selector that stopped matching cannot pass by comparing nothing to nothing. THAT GUARD EXISTS BECAUSE THE TEST WAS ONCE FALSELY GREEN in exactly that way - its header records that a plain indexOf matched the selector inside a PROSE COMMENT and returned the LIGHT palette for every dark case, for the file's entire life until 2026-08-10. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, AND IT IS HALF THE REQUIREMENT. Every one of the 20 pairs is asserted at 4.5:1. NOT ONE uses the 3:1 threshold, so the requirement's 'large text and UI components' clause has no case at all - no border-on-background pair, no focus-ring pair, no disabled-state pair. And the four states the requirement names by name - normal, hover, focused, disabled - are absent from the pair table entirely; tokens.css contains only six focus, hover or disabled mentions in total. SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN THE REQUIREMENT TOO: the file's own header says it covers 'the design tokens the Topics screens rely on', not the application. AND THE RENDERED QUESTION IS UNTOUCHED BY DESIGN: color-contrast is explicitly disabled in BOTH axe passes, the jsdom one because there is no layout engine and the live Playwright one by convention, so nothing anywhere measures contrast as actually painted - only as declared in tokens.

No new dependency, no browser, no new technique - the same file, more rows.

title: NFR-023'S ABSOLUTE-SESSION CEILING IS SATISFIED BY A KEYCLOAK DEFAULT THAT ACMP NEVER CHOSE AND DOES NOT PIN. AC-139 records NFR-023 Met, and the idle half of that verdict is solid - thirty-minute app-side inactivity detection, built deliberately under OQ-076, mutation-tested, 100 percent covered. THE ABSOLUTE HALF IS DIFFERENT IN KIND AND THIS ROW EXISTS TO SAY SO. The clause is that refresh tokens shall not extend a session beyond twenty-four hours without re-authentication, and what satisfies it is ssoSessionMaxLifespan, measured at 36000 seconds - ten hours - on the LIVE PRODUCTION realm via kcadm on 2026-08-13. Ten hours is comfortably inside twenty-four. But deploy/keycloak/realm-export.json sets NEITHER ssoSessionIdleTimeout NOR ssoSessionMaxLifespan: a grep for either key across every json and shell file in the repository returns nothing. So the value is not ACMP's decision at all - it is whatever the Keycloak image defaults to, observed once, eight days before this row was written. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY WOULD FAIL IF IT CHANGED. A Keycloak image bump could raise the maximum lifespan past twenty-four hours and every test, every gate and every acceptance criterion would stay green, because none of them reads it. This is the same shape as NFR-050: a property that is TRUE across everything measured, and GUARDED by nothing - except that NFR-050's property is a fact about migrations already written, while this one is a fact about a third party's default that can change under a version bump. TWO FURTHER THINGS WORTH KEEPING TOGETHER HERE, because they are the same configuration surface. First, realm-export.json reaches FRESH stacks only, which this project has already been bitten by - so pinning the values there fixes new environments and does nothing for the running ones, and reconcile.sh is the only seam to those. Second, OQ-003's resolution names a 60-minute idle timeout while the realm and the application both implement 30; that inconsistency is recorded inside OQ-076 and is harmless against NFR-023's ceilings, but anyone pinning these values should settle which number is intended rather than pinning whichever one they happen to read first.
activation_trigger: Whenever the Keycloak image is next bumped - that is the exact moment an unpinned default can change underneath the requirement, and it is also when someone is already editing the realm configuration. Also fires if a fresh environment is ever stood up, since a fresh stack inherits the image default rather than an ACMP decision, and immediately if anyone proposes changing the app-side idle timeout, because the two halves need to stay coherent. CHEAPEST FIRST STEP: add ssoSessionIdleTimeout and ssoSessionMaxLifespan to realm-export.json with the values that were measured, so a fresh stack gets ACMP's numbers rather than the image's. That alone converts an inherited default into a stated decision. The reconcile path is the separate half - realm-export.json reaches FRESH stacks only, so an existing environment needs reconcile.sh to carry the same values or the two drift.

title: NFR-019 IS KEPT AS THE TARGET AND TWO OF ITS THREE HOPS RUN PLAINTEXT: THIS IS THAT GAP, TRACKED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED. Operator disposition DEC-066, 2026-08-20: NFR-019 stays as written and this row carries the divergence. WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNENCRYPTED, measured. deploy/nginx/cloud-443.conf.template proxies to http://keycloak:8080/ at line 121 and to http://api:8080 at line 145; deploy/nginx/default.conf.template does the same for dev at line 58; and KeycloakAdmin__BaseUrl defaults to http://keycloak:8080/ in BOTH compose files. So everything behind the reverse proxy speaks unencrypted HTTP over the Docker network. WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, and should not be re-done by whoever takes this: the PUBLIC edge is configured exactly to the floor NFR-019 states - cloud-443.conf.template line 30 sets ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3, with certificates published by certbot-deploy-hook.sh - and the application-to-SQL-Server hop is encrypted, the connection string carrying Encrypt=True. The Tarseem hop the requirement names has no endpoint at all: P14 was deferred indefinitely by DEC-028 and a repository-wide search for the name returns one hit, a placeholder page. So the work is the Keycloak and api hops, not all three. TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS LARGER THAN A CONFIG EDIT. First, service-to-service TLS needs a certificate story - who issues, who rotates, and what each container trusts - and the existing certbot flow does not extend to it, because those certificates are for a public hostname while these services address each other by compose service name. Second, the VERSION FLOOR is unpinned everywhere except the public edge: no SslProtocols setting, no MinProtocol, no ssl_protocols directive exists on any internal hop, so even after TLS is introduced the 'TLS 1.0 and 1.1 shall be disabled' clause would still rest on image defaults - the same shape as DW-073, where NFR-023's absolute ceiling is satisfied by a Keycloak default nobody chose. WHY THIS IS A DEFERRED-WORK ROW AND NFR-019 HAS NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: the requirement cannot record Met while two of the hops it names are plaintext, and an AC recording Partial would hold package readiness false permanently because acs-met counts by retired_in and ignores lifecycle_status. NFR-019 sits exactly where NFR-054 sits behind DW-066 - deliberately unverifiable, with the register stating the target rather than the status quo. DO NOT LET A LATER SESSION ADD THE MISSING CRITERION.
activation_trigger: Whenever the deployment stops being single-host - the moment any of these services moves to a different machine, a plaintext hop crosses a real network and this becomes urgent rather than tracked. Also fires if an external security review or the NFR-018 ASVS assessment examines transport security, since this is exactly what such a review looks for; and whenever nginx or Keycloak is next reconfigured, because that is when the certificate plumbing is already open. ⚠ DO NOT START THIS AS A SIDE EFFECT OF SOMETHING ELSE: it needs a certificate story for service-to-service trust (who issues, who rotates, what the containers trust) and that is a design decision, not a config edit. title: ToastProvider IS BUILT, TESTED AND MOUNTED NOWHERE - the app has a transient-feedback mechanism no feature can use. Found 2026-08-21 while building WBS-23.3's PNG export, which needed exactly this and could not have it. `src/components/ui/Toast.tsx` exports a full `ToastProvider` (portalled `aria-live="polite"` region, queue, 5s auto-dismiss, three tones, dismiss button) and a `useToast()` hook that THROWS 'useToast must be used within a ToastProvider' when no provider is above it. A repository-wide search for `ToastProvider` and `useToast` outside the component's own file returns exactly one file: `overlays.test.tsx`, its own test. So the provider is never mounted in the application tree, `useToast()` would throw from any real screen, and the component's own doc comment cites Design System section 12 for a mechanism the product cannot reach. It arrived in the big design-fidelity import (`16f2f8b`, PR #9) alongside the rest of the shared component library and nothing has wired it since. THIS IS THE 'already half-built' SHAPE the project keeps meeting, and it is worth stating precisely: the component is NOT dead code in the usual sense - it is correct, covered and ready - it is simply unreachable, and a green test suite over a component nobody mounts says nothing about whether the app has toasts. WHAT WBS-23.3 DID INSTEAD, so this row is not read as a defect against that build: PNG-export failure feedback is rendered inline in the card as a `.rpt-card-note` with `role="status"`, reusing a class that already exists. That is the right call for one button - mounting an app-wide provider to give one feature a failure message would be a far larger change than the feature - but it is the SECOND ad-hoc transient-feedback treatment in this codebase and a third will make the inconsistency the real cost. NOT SIZED AS TRIVIAL, because the interesting part is not the mount. Wiring `ToastProvider` into the app shell is a few lines; deciding WHICH existing ad-hoc confirmations and failure notices should become toasts, and localising `regionLabel` (it currently defaults to the untranslated English string 'Notifications'), is the actual work, and it touches screens across several modules.
activation_trigger: EITHER of two events, and the first is the more likely: (a) a third feature needs transient success/failure feedback and is about to invent a third ad-hoc treatment - at that point the inconsistency is established and wiring the provider is cheaper than the third bespoke one; or (b) a design-fidelity or accessibility pass takes up Design System section 12, which the component's own header cites. NOT triggered by the component merely existing unmounted - it costs nothing where it sits, breaks nothing, and this row exists so that fact is recorded rather than rediscovered. ⚠ Whoever activates it must localise `regionLabel`, which today defaults to a hardcoded English 'Notifications' and would ship an untranslated accessible name into an aria-live region the moment the provider is mounted.

TopicSource IS A NINE-VALUE DOMAIN VOCABULARY THAT NO SURFACE IN THE PRODUCT HAS EVER SHOWN OR OFFERED, AND IT HAS NO BILINGUAL LABELS AT ALL. Found 2026-08-21 while building WBS-23.4, which needed to decide whether the reclassify dialog should offer a source picker beside the type picker. THE FACTS, checked rather than assumed: `TopicSource` declares nine values (CommitteeMember, StreamRequest, UrgentOrgNeed, OperationalIncident, SecurityFinding, Modernization, InnovationInitiative, CrossStreamProblem, Regulatory). `SubmitTopic.tsx` sends a hardcoded `SOURCE_DEFAULT` and its own header records that as a P5a decision - the submitter never chooses one. A search of both locale bundles for any of the nine names returns ZERO keys; the only hit anywhere is `audit.entity.CommitteeMember`, which is a different vocabulary that happens to share a word. So every topic in the product carries a source, the domain and the API both take it, and no human has ever seen or set one.

WHY WBS-23.4 DID NOT ADD THE PICKER, so this is not read as an oversight. Exposing source means authoring EIGHTEEN new strings - nine English and nine Arabic - for governance concepts, and the Arabic half is the problem: NFR-039 requires a single canonical source of bilingual terms, LL-010 records that the glossary it names is a circular pointer between two English documents and does not exist, and DW-069 carries building it. Inventing nine Arabic governance terms inside a feature slice is exactly what that requirement forbids, and it would seed terminology the glossary would later have to either bless or contradict. The reclassify endpoint therefore takes BOTH fields, because the domain method does and the API is the contract; the SPA sends the topic's existing source back unchanged.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BLOCKED AND WHAT IS NOT. The API is NOT blocked - a caller can already correct a source today through POST /api/topics/{id}/reclassify, and AC-143 says so while deliberately not claiming a UI for it. What is blocked is the UI, and only on the terminology.
activation_trigger: EITHER: (a) DW-069's bilingual glossary exists and can supply the nine Arabic terms, at which point this is a small picker beside the type one and the strings are a transcription rather than an invention; or (b) a Secretary reports that a topic's source is wrong and cannot be corrected in-product - the same demand-shaped trigger DW-032 carried, and the operator is the demand channel it names. ⚠ NOT triggered by the field merely being invisible: it has been invisible since v1, nothing depends on it being visible, and the endpoint already accepts corrections. ⚠ Whoever activates it must ALSO decide whether source becomes visible on read surfaces (topic detail, backlog facets), because a field a user can set but not see afterwards is worse than one they can do neither with.

EVERY DIALOG THAT PAIRS A DESCRIPTION WITH A FORM FIELD RENDERS THE FIRST FIELD LABEL FLUSH AGAINST THE DESCRIPTION - a shared design-system spacing gap, NOT a defect in any one screen. `Dialog.tsx` renders the description and then `{children}` with nothing between them; `.dialog-desc` carries `margin: 0`, and `.field` only gets top spacing from `.field + .field`, which by definition cannot apply to the FIRST field. So the first label always sits directly under the description's last line.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and this is the part worth copying. WBS-23.4's new reclassify dialog looked cramped in a browser check - the kind of thing JSDOM cannot see. Rather than fix it locally or change shared CSS on a hunch, the SHIPPED convert dialog was rendered in the same harness as a CONTROL, and it has the identical spacing. That settled it by evidence: the new dialog MATCHES the application rather than introducing anything, so changing it alone would have made it the inconsistent one.

SIZING, measured rather than guessed. The fix is one rule - roughly `.dialog-desc + .field { margin-block-start: var(--sp-4) }` in `overlays.css`. The COST is not the rule, it is the verification: `<Field>` renders `.field`, so around twenty dialogs across actions, decisions, dependencies, governance, meetings, research, risks, administration and topics would all shift, and a design-system spacing change wants each of them looked at rather than a green suite. That is a design pass, not a feature slice - which is why WBS-23.4 shipped consistent with the other twenty instead of folding it in. Precedent: DW-022 deferred SPA style hygiene on the same reasoning.
activation_trigger: A frontend consistency or design-system pass takes it on - the same trigger DW-022 carries, and the two should be done together since both are dialog/field styling. ⚠ NOT triggered by any single dialog looking cramped: that is the shared behaviour, and fixing one screen in isolation is what this row exists to prevent. ⚠ Whoever does it must re-verify the ~20 affected dialogs VISUALLY, not by suite - the whole finding came from looking at one, and a green test suite reported nothing wrong with any of them.

BUILD THE OWASP ASVS 5.0 LEVEL 2 EVIDENCE PACK FOR NFR-018 - AN INPUT TO AN ASSESSMENT, NOT THE ASSESSMENT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ROW. NFR-018 (Must, Approved) requires the application to meet OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2 for all applicable chapters. It is the ONLY remaining requirement that real work could close, and it cannot be closed from inside this repository: Level 2 conformance is established by an external assessor, not by self-assertion. This row produces the document that maps the controls THIS CODEBASE ALREADY HAS to the L2 chapters, so an assessor does not start cold and does not bill for rediscovering what is already built.

WHY IT EXISTS AS AN OVERRIDE, recorded so nobody reads it as a settled judgement. The agent recommended leaving NFR-018 alone: it is blocked on a third party, no trigger had fired, and preparation without a consumer is speculative work. The operator chose 'Prepare the evidence pack now' (DEC-072 d4), on the view that an assessor starting cold is a cost paid later at worse rates.

WHAT THIS ROW MUST NOT BECOME, and a later session will be tempted. IT DOES NOT CLOSE NFR-018. The requirement stays Approved and correctly carries NO acceptance criterion, because acs-met counts by retired_in and ignores lifecycle_status, so an AC written ahead of an assessor's report would hold package readiness false forever (trap 16c). DO NOT write an acceptance criterion for NFR-018 out of this pack, and do not let the pack's own completeness be mistaken for conformance - a map of existing controls to chapters is a claim about coverage of the DOCUMENT, never about the adequacy of the controls, which is precisely the judgement an assessor is paid to make.

WHAT THE PACK SHOULD CARRY, and much of it already exists as evidence in this package. The authorization model and its per-request revalidation (ADR-0039, AC-090), the deny-by-default read gate (DEF-052's GuestSurfaceMiddleware), the hash-linked immutable audit chain, the confidentiality ABAC with egress redaction (SL-030, AV-192), secret handling, the session and idle-timeout behaviour (useIdleSignOut.ts), input validation as it is actually enforced - in the DOMAIN for the four commands carrying scalar input, which an endpoint-level census gets wrong (LL-006). IT MUST ALSO CARRY THE KNOWN GAPS HONESTLY, or it is worse than no pack: DEF-100 and DW-074 record that two of NFR-019's three internal hops run plaintext by design, and an assessor will look for exactly that. A pack that omits a gap the register already holds is the manufactured-status move DEF-010 records. ▸▸ DONE 2026-08-29. The pack is DOC-070 at tamheed-package/docs/asvs-l2-evidence-pack.md - the first narrative document in this package to live outside the frozen docs/ archive. THIS ROW'S OWN CLOSING CONDITION IS MET AND NO OTHER: it said the row closes when the pack exists and has been reviewed. ⛔ NFR-018 DID NOT MOVE AND MUST NOT - it stays Approved with NO acceptance criterion, because only an external assessor's report can evidence it and an AC written from this pack would hold package readiness false permanently (trap 16c). Commissioning the assessment remains the operator's act alone. ⚠ FOUR GAPS FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT ARE CARRIED IN THE PACK AND FILED: DW-093 (C-AUTH-05's SoD-4 has no hard guard), DW-092 (C-INS-01's Restricted-access alert), DEF-118 (DOC-067 is stale and its title claims an ASVS mapping its body lacks), and the measured plaintext-hop set of at least four internal endpoints, where DOC-067 and DEF-100/DW-074 each name a different incomplete subset.

THE .NET 8 TO 10 RUNTIME MIGRATION (#128 sdk, #134 aspnet) TOGETHER WITH DW-066's MINIMAL-BASE MOVE, AS ONE BASE-IMAGE DECISION. Carved out of the DW-078 queue sweep by DEC-074 d1 because it is a RUNTIME MIGRATION, not a dependency bump: the solution targets net8.0, so moving to 10.0 touches target frameworks, analyzers, EF Core and the container base at once. Folding it into a hygiene sweep would put a migration underneath every other failure in that batch - the same attribution argument DEC-073 used one level up when it put the sweep before SL-033.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AT ALL, and it is a finding about instruments rather than about .NET. Both pull requests were INVISIBLE when DEC-072 d1 authorised 'sweep everything, majors included', because the gh pr list behind that description carried --limit 10 and these two sat past position ten (PE-599). They are the OLDEST rows in the queue, 2026-07-16, and the listing is newest-first, so the cap truncated exactly the end where the largest and most-aged work lived. THE OPERATOR WAS RE-ASKED WITH THE CORRECTED FACTS RATHER THAN HAVING THE WORD 'EVERYTHING' STRETCHED OVER WORK THEY HAD NEVER SEEN.

WHAT RIDES WITH IT (DEC-074 d2): DW-066's move of api and worker from Debian aspnet:8.0 to alpine or distroless. #134 edits deploy/Dockerfile.backend lines 31 and 51 and #128 edits line 16 - verified with gh pr view --json files, not inferred - and those are precisely the lines DW-066 is about. DW-066's own trigger reads 'whenever a base-image bump is being made anyway (Dependabot docker updates touch these lines)', so the trigger has fired verbatim. Merging #134 alone would spend the expensive part of the change - opening the Dockerfile, running the full e2e leg, re-verifying Arabic FREETEXT - on a Debian-to-Debian move and leave the minimal-base clause exactly where it was, with the next opportunity unknown.

THE RISK IS NOT THE EDIT, AND THIS IS THE PART A GREEN SUITE WILL LIE ABOUT. The Dockerfile change is three FROM lines. Alpine is musl rather than glibc, and this application talks to SQL Server through Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and does culture-aware work in Arabic and English - globalization and native interop are exactly where musl breaks, and ICU behaviour differs. Distroless avoids musl but has no shell, which changes the healthcheck and any entrypoint that shells out. THE FAILURE MODE COMPILES AND UNIT-TESTS PERFECTLY: it is a runtime globalization or native-load error. FULL e2e LEG, and verify Arabic search (FREETEXT, LCID 1025) END TO END before believing any of it. A .NET major on top of that means the migration and the base change can each mask the other, so land them in an order that lets you attribute a failure - runtime first on the existing Debian base, then the base move - rather than in one commit.

WHAT IT UNLOCKS: NFR-054's minimal-base clause becomes evidenceable for the first time. It cannot record Met while api and worker sit on a Debian base, and DW-066 is the only route to an acceptance criterion for that clause. The clause was KEPT rather than relaxed (SC-024, the operator declining the narrowing) precisely so that it would eventually be satisfied rather than argued away. ▸▸ DONE 2026-08-29, BOTH PHASES. Phase A (net8.0 -> net10.0) merged as PR #320 -> df8d7c3a; phase B (the minimal-base decision) as PR #325 -> 1d7cb04b, ten checks green including the e2e leg this row demanded. Executed as WBS-25.1, promoted to Implemented by DEC-092. DEC-090 d1 chose aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra and d2 replaced the shell healthcheck with Acmp.HealthProbe: 326 MB -> 258 MB (-21%), application CVEs 75 -> 11 (-85%), zero criticals either side. ⚠ THE SPIKE FALSIFIED THIS ROW'S OWN PREDICTION and the correction is the durable part: a no-ICU base does NOT throw at runtime here - it starts, exits 0, and silently enters invariant mode, throwing only when a non-invariant culture is TOUCHED, and this API touches none. The real discriminator is the ICU VERSION, not musl. ⛔ THE -extra SUFFIX IS THEREFORE LOAD-BEARING: a digest bump that dropped it would render a Hijri date instead of a Gregorian one in Arabic, with no exception and no log line, and would pass every existing gate. ⚠ RESIDUALS STAY OPEN: DW-090 (no CI check asserts image size or base layer - a size check ALONE would have passed on Debian at 326 MB) and DW-091 (both api dependents use service_started, so nothing consumes the new healthcheck's verdict). NFR-054 stays Approved.

SEC-120 MANDATES 'Minimum 1 approver (lead or peer)' AND THE TEAM IS ONE HUMAN, WHICH MAKES THE CLAUSE UNSATISFIABLE RATHER THAN MERELY UNMET. GitHub forbids self-approval, so configuring required_approving_review_count=1 on main would block every merge this project makes, including its own author's. DEF-105's fix therefore set it to 0: pull requests are required and all nine status checks are required, but no human approval is, and that is the honest maximum for a single-operator repository.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE IN DEF-105: DEF-105's claim was that no branch protection existed, and that claim is now false, so the row is Fixed. title:
VISUAL-VERIFY HARNESSES LEAK AS PROCESSES AND NOTHING TEARS THEM DOWN - trap 28 GUARDS THE FILES AND MISSES THE PROCESSES, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY SIX SURVIVED THIRTEEN DAYS. Found 2026-08-23: six vite dev servers plus their six npx parents, all rooted in src/Acmp.Web/node_modules, on ports 5199, 5201, 5233, 5241, 4173 and 8124, started across 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-21 by earlier sessions' visual-verify work - two of them carrying a .vp argument, which is the tell. They held rolldown-binding.win32-x64-msvc.node open, so npm ci and npm install failed on the host with EPERM and EBUSY, and an npm ci that unlinks node_modules before reinstalling gutted the tree from 171 packages to 35 partway through. Killing exactly those twelve restored npm ci to a clean exit and 171 packages, verified by running it rather than assumed.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW RATHER THAN A ONE-OFF CLEANUP: trap 28 already says to delete throwaway visual-verify harnesses before committing, because vr-out/ is gitignored but a vr-*.tsx in src/ is not and would ship. THAT GUARD IS ABOUT FILES. The visual-verify loop also starts a long-lived dev server, and nothing anywhere stops it. A file-level check runs clean over a machine with six leaked servers on it, which is precisely what happened - the working tree was clean all along.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS, and this is the part that cost real time: the failure does not present as leaked processes. It presents as npm refusing to install with an opaque Windows EPERM on a native binary, in a session that has nothing to do with visual verification, days or weeks later. The diagnosis requires enumerating node processes and matching their command lines against the repo path, which nobody does by default. A leaked process is a booby trap with a long fuse and no label.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT: the loop that STARTS a visual-verify server should be the thing that stops it - a trap or finally that kills the pid it launched, or a fixed port plus a pre-flight kill of anything already on it, so a crashed session cannot leave one behind. A cleanup step that lives only in a checklist is the same shape as the branch-protection claim DEF-105 recorded: a control that exists in prose and not in machinery. ⚠ The check must also be able to FAIL LOUDLY: a sweep that finds no leaked servers and one that cannot see them look identical, which is trap 31.
activation_trigger: Whenever a visual-verify harness is next started - that is the moment the teardown belongs, and the cheapest fix is to make starting and stopping one operation rather than two. Also fires immediately if npm ci or npm install fails again on this machine with EPERM or EBUSY on a file under node_modules: enumerate node processes, match their command lines against the repo path, and read this row before debugging npm. ⚠ DO NOT treat that failure as an npm bug or a corrupted lockfile - it is a file lock held by a process from a previous session, and npm ci makes it WORSE by unlinking node_modules before it discovers it cannot finish.

DONE (PR `#309` -> `eb09342`, 2026-08-25). A CONTAINER-STARTUP TIMEOUT NOW BOUNDS EVERY CONTAINER START IN `Acmp.Integration.Tests`, SO A HUNG CONTAINER FAILS FAST WITH ITS OWN LOG ATTACHED INSTEAD OF BURNING THE BACKEND JOB'S 25-MINUTE CEILING AND REPORTING `cancelled`. `DEC-077` d4/d5 - it ran FIRST, before `WBS-24.1`, as ordered.

WHAT SHIPPED. `ContainerStartup.StartOrFailFastAsync` wraps `StartAsync` in a 10-minute `CancellationTokenSource` and, on expiry, throws a `TimeoutException` naming the container, the bound it exceeded, and the tail of the container's own startup log. THREE call sites route through it - `SqlBackstopFixture`, `SearchProvidersFtsTests`, `MinioFileStoreTests`. The row named one fixture, but all three carried the identical unbounded call, and guarding only the reported path would have left the siblings broken. The bound is DELIBERATELY GENEROUS: it covers pull + create + boot + wait strategy, and a bound tight enough to fire on a slow-but-healthy start would manufacture exactly the red `DEC-077` d3 turns into a mandatory operator stop. A whole green backend job runs in about 9 minutes, so 10 still converts a 25-minute `cancelled` into a fast, named failure.

WHY A BOUND ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE SATISFIED THIS ROW - MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Testcontainers' own exception is a `TimeoutException` carrying the message 'The operation has timed out.' - no container, no bound, no log. Setting `TestcontainersSettings.WaitStrategyTimeout` would have stopped the hang and still told nobody what hung, which is the half the `cancelled` verdict actually cost.

PROVEN BY FORCING IT, as this row required, and not by a green run. `ContainerStartupTimeoutTests` first warms the image with a container that DOES become ready - the positive control, and it keeps the cold image pull out of the measured window, because a pull inside it would fire the budget before the container existed and the log tail would silently fall back to a placeholder - then starts one that never satisfies its wait strategy and asserts BOTH halves: the failure names the bound, AND it carries the marker the container printed. BOTH ASSERTIONS ARE MUTATION-PROVEN: dropping the log attachment fails the marker assertion; rethrowing the raw exception fails the bound assertion against 'The operation has timed out.'.

THE SECOND MUTATION IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING, because it is a hollow pass caught before it shipped: asserting the exception TYPE alone would have passed VACUOUSLY, since the framework already throws `TimeoutException` on cancellation. The message assertions are the only part of that test doing work.

WHAT DONE DOES NOT MEAN. It does NOT close `DEF-108`, which stays Open at high severity with package readiness deliberately FALSE (`DEC-077` d1). This changes how the failure PRESENTS; it does not explain why SQLPAL failed to start, and it cannot.

RESIDUAL, filed as `DW-085`: `_image.CreateAsync()` - the FTS image BUILD in the same fixture - is still unbounded, and is now the one remaining unbounded await on that path.

THE DISTINCTION THAT WAS MISSED, because it is the transferable half. The objection is to OWNING a hanging Dockerfile - a file sitting in `deploy/` that looks like a shipped artifact and that someone could build by accident. A build and a start can both be slow in one run: 8 + 10 = 18 minutes still leaves the backend job room under its own `timeout-minutes: 25` to fail, report and finish. title:
THE CALENDAR CANNOT SHOW TOPIC TITLES IN THE GRID BECAUSE `/meetings` CARRIES NO TOPIC IDS - only `/meetings/{key}` does. A lightweight endpoint returning agenda topic ids per meeting would let the month grid render topics directly instead of counts. Residual of `WBS-24.2`, recorded rather than built.

THE GAP, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `MeetingSummary` carries `scheduledStart` and `itemCount` and nothing about which topics are on the agenda; `AgendaItem.topicId` and `topicTitle` live only on `MeetingDetail`, behind `/meetings/{key}`. So a grid that showed topic titles on each day would need one detail request per meeting in the visible month, and each of those responses also carries attendance, discussions and the recording - a heavy payload fetched for two string fields.

WHAT `WBS-24.2` DID INSTEAD, so this row is not read as a defect in that work. The grid answers `FR-035`'s purpose clause - *see how topics are spread across upcoming meetings* - from ONE request, using the per-meeting count; selecting a meeting then fetches THAT ONE meeting's topics. `AC-145` states the exclusion explicitly rather than quietly covering less than its criterion. The design's day cells hold two or three chips before they overflow anyway, so titles-in-grid was never obviously the better rendering.

WHAT WOULD MOVE THIS ROW. A concrete ask for topic titles visible in the month grid without selecting a meeting - at which point the cheapest honest answer is a projection on the Meetings side returning `{meetingId, scheduledStart, items: [{topicId, topicKey, topicTitle}]}`, which is a backend change and belongs in a slice rather than in a frontend batch. ⚠ Do NOT solve it by fanning out `useMeetingDetail` across the month: that is the N+1 shape, and `DEF-104` is this project's record of what unbounded read patterns cost. ▸▸ ACTIVATED 2026-08-29 by DEC-094 / SC-038, and scheduled as WBS-26.5 in SL-035. ⚠ THIS WAS AN OVERRIDE: the agent recommended carrying this row Open, and the reasoning-against is preserved in DEC-094 so the activation is not later read as agreement (DEC-071 d3's precedent). ⚠ ACTIVATION DOES NOT CREATE AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION - one written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently (trap 16c), so the criterion is written in the batch that produces the evidence. ⛔ DO NOT FAN useMeetingDetail ACROSS THE MONTH - the row's own prohibition survives activation and is not softened by it; that is DEF-104's N+1 shape. ⚠ DEC-094 d7 ruled this a REFINEMENT BEYOND a satisfied requirement: FR-035 stays Implemented, this work advances no requirement and owes no criterion against it.
activation_trigger: Fires when someone asks to see topic TITLES in the calendar month grid without selecting a meeting first - that is the moment the per-meeting count stops being enough. It also fires if another surface needs topics-by-meeting-date in bulk, since the same projection would serve both. It is NOT fired by WBS-24.2's delivery: AC-145 covers the count-in-grid plus titles-on-selection deliberately, and the requirement's purpose clause is satisfied. Done when the Meetings module exposes a lightweight per-meeting agenda projection and the calendar reads it, with the N+1 fan-out explicitly not used.

title:
CONTROL `C-INS-01`'s BULK-EXPORT-VOLUME ALERT NOW HAS A LIVE SUBJECT AND NOTHING BEHIND IT - `WBS-24.6` FALSIFIED THE SENTENCE THAT JUSTIFIED NOT BUILDING IT.

WHAT THE DOCUMENT SAYS. `SEC-248` lists what is deliberately NOT alertable in v1, *"stated, not silently skipped"*, and its first entry is bulk/atypical export volume: *"named in `C-INS-01`: **ACMP has no export feature.** Traceability-matrix export (CSV/Excel) is deferred to Phase 3 (`D-07`), and no other endpoint emits a bulk download. There is nothing to alert on; this signal activates with `D-07`, not before. Writing a rule now would create a tripwire that can never fire."*

WHY THAT REASONING WAS SOUND AND IS NOW SPENT. It was not an oversight - it was a correctly argued exclusion, and the argument turned entirely on the premise that no endpoint emits a bulk download. `WBS-24.6` adds one, and it adds it on the most sensitive dataset in the product. **The alert's activation condition was `D-07`; what actually fired it was a different row entirely**, which is why nothing noticed: the trigger named a Phase-3 item, not a property of the system, so the row could not see its own condition being met from another direction.

WHAT THE THREAT MODEL EXPECTS. `SEC-329` `T-10` and `SEC-330` `AB-6` are both mass-export exfiltration, rated moderate likelihood and HIGH impact, and both list `C-INS-01` - *"anomaly alert / optional dual-control on bulk/atypical export volume"* - as a named mitigation alongside `C-API-02` (export scoped by role), `C-AUDIT-08` (export audited as a sensitive event) and `C-API-03` (rate limiting). **`WBS-24.6` delivers the other three.** Role scoping comes from `Policies.AuditRead` plus `Policies.ReportExport`; the audited sensitive event carrying who, scope and volume is built; and an export rate-limit policy is added to the existing per-user fixed-window limiter. `C-INS-01` is the one mitigation of the four that this item does NOT deliver, and saying so plainly is the point of this row.

WHY IT IS DEFERRED RATHER THAN BUILT. Anomaly detection needs a baseline, and there is none - the endpoint ships with zero usage history, so any threshold chosen today would be a guess dressed as a control, which is the shape this project keeps finding in instruments. The audit event this item emits already RECORDS the volume, so the data the alert would consume starts accumulating immediately and a threshold can be set from evidence later. Alerting also belongs to the ops/runtime group that is separately blocked on a running stack.

⚠ AND `SEC-248` ITSELF IS NOW WRONG AND IS NOT EDITED HERE. Its sentence *"ACMP has no export feature"* is false from the moment `WBS-24.6` merges. It is left in place deliberately: the narrative documents are the planner's record of what was decided when, and this row is the correction. **A reader who finds that sentence and not this row would conclude the gap is intentional and still argued for.** ▸▸ ACTIVATED 2026-08-29 by DEC-094 / SC-038, and scheduled as WBS-26.2 in SL-035. ⚠ THIS WAS AN OVERRIDE: the agent recommended carrying this row Open, and the reasoning-against is preserved in DEC-094 so the activation is not later read as agreement (DEC-071 d3's precedent). ⚠ ACTIVATION DOES NOT CREATE AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION - one written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently (trap 16c), so the criterion is written in the batch that produces the evidence. Built as ONE UNIT with DW-092, its Restricted-access sibling. ⚠ The agent's recommendation to carry rested on there being no baseline from which to choose a threshold, and that objection is unchanged by activation - it is now work to solve, not a reason to wait.

✅✅ **DONE - BUILT AS `WBS-26.2`, PR `#331` → `c273294c`, 2026-08-30.** `Audit.BulkExportAnomaly` fires when a delivered export row count reaches the configured threshold, as a SECOND event beside the C-AUDIT-08 record rather than in place of it; `AC-157` `Met` (`AV-235`), `NFR-065` → `Implemented`. ⭐ **THE BASELINE OBJECTION WAS RESOLVED RATHER THAN WAITED OUT**, and that is the part worth carrying: `NFR-065`'s second clause requires the BASIS of each threshold to be recorded as *derived from observed usage* or *provisional pending a baseline*, so **provisional is a legitimate recorded answer** and the control can exist while evidence accumulates. The value lives in the `ConfigurationSetting` store, not in code, so it is replaceable without a deployment (`DEC-099` d3; `DEF-110` is the record of the alternative). ⚠ The Seq alert RULE that would notify on this event is NOT built - `DEC-099` d2 puts detection in the app and notification in Seq, and that half belongs to the ops group. ⚠ `DW-095` records that C-INS-01 names FIVE signals and this pair is two of them.
activation_trigger:
EITHER of two conditions, and they are genuinely independent.

FIRST - enough audit-export usage exists to set a threshold from evidence rather than from a guess. The `C-AUDIT-08` event `WBS-24.6` emits carries actor, filter scope and row volume for every export, so the baseline builds itself; the condition is met when that history can distinguish a normal export from an atypical one. This is the cheap path and it is the intended one.

SECOND - any release sign-off that wants to claim the `T-10` / `AB-6` mitigations are in place. Three of the four named mitigations ship with `WBS-24.6` and this is the fourth; a sign-off asserting the set is complete would be asserting something false. ⚠ This clause is NOT the same as the release-sign-off clauses in `DW-041`, `DW-067` and `DW-071`, which `DEC-071` d4 parked - those concern accessibility conformance claims. This one concerns a HIGH-impact threat-model mitigation, and it should be judged on its own terms rather than swept up with them.

⛔ DO NOT read the arrival of a second export endpoint as a third trigger. `D-07`, the traceability-matrix export, is still Phase 3 and its arrival changes the volume of exports, not whether the signal has a subject - that question is already settled by `WBS-24.6`.

title: THE TOPIC-ATTACHMENT DOWNLOAD BUTTON IS RENDERED AND INERT, AND NO REGISTER ROW HAS EVER COVERED IT. TopicDetail.tsx renders a per-attachment download button that is hardcoded `disabled` with a `topics.comingSoon` title, beside the honest source comment 'Download needs a presigned-URL endpoint not exposed in this DTO yet -> inert, flagged'. So the flag was raised in the ONE place no register view can read, which is the DEF-101 and OQ-DATA shape: a prose-only marker that every mechanical control runs straight over. MEASURED, not inferred, and with controls in both directions. There are exactly TWO production callers of IFileStore.GetPreSignedUrlAsync in the whole solution: GetRecordingUrl.cs for meeting recordings, and TopicReader.GetMaterialUrlAsync, which is reached ONLY through the /session/materials/{attachmentId} handler and is caller-scoped to a guest presenter's own slot. src/Acmp.Web/src/api/topics.ts contains an UPLOAD helper and no download call at all. A sweep of the deferred-work register for the concept returned ZERO covering rows against a control of 27 rows matching the word topic, so this is not a duplicate. THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this is worth a row rather than a shrug: a Chairman, Secretary, Member, Reviewer or Auditor can see that a topic has attachments, can read their names, sizes and uploader, and CANNOT OPEN ANY OF THEM ANYWHERE IN THE PRODUCT. The only principal who can open a topic attachment is a GUEST PRESENTER, and only for the single topic on their own agenda slot. That is an inverted capability gradient that nothing in the package states as intended, and it is invisible to every register view because the disabled attribute makes the button render correctly and no test asserts that a committee member can retrieve a file. WHY THIS IS A DEFERRED-WORK ROW AND NOT A DEFECT: nothing is broken against a written requirement. The button is honestly disabled rather than throwing, the comment tells the truth, and no acceptance criterion claims committee-side download works. An acceptance criterion written today would have to evidence a retrieval path that does not exist, which is the trap 16c failure. FOUND while sizing WBS-24.8, where an early draft of the plan asserted that Chairman and Secretary could already open a presenter's materials from the topic page and therefore that withholding an open control in the preview cost them nothing. THAT ASSERTION WAS FALSE and the measurement above is what caught it, before the operator ruled on it.
activation_trigger: Fires when any of three things happens. FIRST, and most likely: if WBS-24.8's preview ships an open control over a targeted presenter's materials, then the product gains a non-guest pre-signed download path, and this row's gap becomes an inconsistency rather than a uniform absence - the committee can open a file through a preview of somebody else's view but not through the topic that owns it. title: NOTHING MAKES A WORK ITEM NAME THE CRITERIA IT SATISFIED, SO AN ITEM CAN BE MERGED, VERDICTED AND LEFT PERMANENTLY UNREVIEWABLE. scripts/gen-slice-review-slate.mjs derives a work item's acceptance criteria by regex over the item's own title, and its comment states the assumption plainly: 'A completion record names its criterion; anything else is a guess, and a guess is a hole.' That assumption is a CONVENTION and nothing enforces it. Measured across SL-033 on 2026-08-29: WBS-24.1, 24.2, 24.3, 24.6 and 24.7 name one criterion each, WBS-24.4 names two, WBS-24.5 names three - and WBS-24.8 named NONE until it was amended by hand in that session, because its title was still the original specification text and the completion amendment every earlier item had received was never applied. THE FAILURE MODE, WHICH IS NARROW BUT REAL: an item ships, its criteria are verdicted Met, its requirement auto-advances, and its row still describes work rather than recording completion. Every register view is satisfied - ids resolve, statuses are consistent, G-TRACE passes - because a status is not an id and no gate reads titles for this. The absence only surfaces when somebody tries to hold a review, which may be long after the fact or never. WHY IT IS A DEFERRED-WORK ROW RATHER THAN A DEFECT OR AN IMMEDIATE FIX: the damage is bounded and the bound is deliberate. Since DEF-116 the generator fails CLOSED and LOUDLY on an item naming no criterion, so a review cannot be held in ignorance - the operator gets an abort, not a page with a hole in it. What remains is that the abort arrives LATE, after merge and after verdicts, and that an item nobody ever reviews is never noticed at all. That is a gap worth recording and not worth a gate today. ⚠ THE CHEAPEST FORM IF IT IS EVER BUILT is a package-side scan rather than a new CI gate: enumerate wbs-item rows in a terminal or Review status whose slice has bound acceptance criteria, and report any whose title names none. It must fail on an implausibly small subject set, because a scan that finds nothing over zero rows is the shape this project keeps finding in its own instruments.
activation_trigger: Fires on either of two conditions. FIRST, and the likely one: a second occurrence - any work item reaching a terminal status while its row names no acceptance criterion. One instance is a convention nobody wrote down; two is a convention nobody follows, and the second is the point at which a check earns itself. SECOND: any change to how slice reviews are produced or adjudicated - a new generator, a different review prompt, or a decision to review at a scope other than the slice - since each of those either inherits this assumption or replaces it, and inheriting it silently is how it survived unexamined until DEF-116. ⚠ IT DOES NOT FIRE ON A CLEAN REVIEW. The generator aborting loudly is this gap being CONTAINED rather than being discovered, and treating a successful containment as an activation would schedule work every time the safeguard did its job.

A size check alone would have passed on Debian at 326 MB, reporting compliance with a MINIMAL-BASE clause from the base that clause excludes. And `DEC-090`'s spike measured that plain chiseled and plain alpine ship no ICU, and that a .NET app on them starts, exits 0, and throws only when a non-invariant culture is TOUCHED - which this API never does - so a digest bump silently dropping `-extra` would render a Hijri date instead of a Gregorian one in Arabic, with no exception and no log line, passing every existing gate.

⛔⛔ **THIS ROW'S SKETCH OF THE CHECK WAS WRONG IN THREE WAYS AND WAS CORRECTED IN PLACE BY `DEC-102` BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN.** The superseded sketch read: *"after the compose build in CI, docker image inspect the api and worker images, assert Size <= 500 MB each, and assert the base layer is the pinned chiseled-extra digest rather than merely that the build succeeded."* **(1)** THREE images, not two - `NFR-054` names `api`, `worker` AND `web`; a check built to the sketch would have evidenced two-thirds of the requirement it exists to make evidenceable. **(2)** The expected base is PER-IMAGE, not one digest - `api`/`worker` are `aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra`, `web` is `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.31-alpine`. **(3)** THERE WAS NO COMPOSE BUILD IN CI: the `compose` job ran `docker compose config -q` plus node checks and built nothing; `publish` builds all four but is gated on push-to-main AND `vars.AWS_ROLE_ARN != ''` and reported `skipped`; `security.yml`'s `trivy-image` builds `api` alone. **An inspect step attached to a job that builds nothing can, on a warm runner, SUCCEED against a leftover image - reporting compliance it never measured, which is precisely the failure this row was filed about.** ⭐ The CENSUS in this row was exact and only the REMEDY was too small - `LL-025`'s shape, invisible to every mechanical pass because every identifier resolved and every status was correct.

The expectation is deliberately not derived from the Dockerfile, so a DIGEST bump needs no edit and a REPO:TAG change fails until a human edits the table.
