CONTROL `C-INS-01`'s SECOND DECLINED SIGNAL - ATYPICAL `Restricted`-TOPIC ACCESS - NOW HAS A LIVE SUBJECT AND NOTHING RECORDS IT. `DW-087` IS ITS SIBLING AND COVERS ONLY THE OTHER HALF.

WHAT THE DOCUMENT SAYS. `DOC-067` (`docs/validation/security-controls-audit.md`) lists two `C-INS-01` anomaly-alert signals as *"deliberately NOT written (recorded rather than silently skipped)"*, and gives one reason for each: bulk/atypical export volume, because *"ACMP has no export feature (D-07, Phase 3)"*; and atypical `Restricted`-topic access, because *"no confidentiality tier exists (D-20)"*. It closes: *"A rule for either would be a tripwire that can never fire."*

BOTH PREMISES ARE NOW FALSE, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS RECORDED ANYWHERE. `DW-087` handles the export half in full - `WBS-24.6` shipped the audit-log export and that row says so, names the three of four `T-10`/`AB-6` mitigations the item delivered, and explains why the alert is deferred rather than built. THIS ROW IS THE OTHER HALF. `SL-030` shipped Confidentiality ABAC for Restricted topics with egress redaction (`AV-192`, mutation-proven), so the confidentiality tier the exclusion turned on EXISTS: measured 2026-08-29, `Confidentiality` resolves across ten or more C# files including `ConfidentialityRequirement.cs`, `ITopicConfidentiality.cs` and `AbacProviders.cs`, against a control sweep that was non-zero in the same pass. The tripwire that could never fire now has something to fire on.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT SOONER. A two-key register sweep run while sizing `WBS-25.2`: rows matching a confidentiality/Restricted key AND an alert/anomaly/detection key returned ZERO across deferred-work, defects, open-questions, requirements, decisions, risks and ADRs, while the control term `Restricted` alone returned non-zero in six of those seven registers - so the sweep is proven to have had subjects and the zero is an absence rather than a broken scan (`LL-013`, `LL-015`). `DW-087` does not cover it: that row is scrupulously scoped to bulk export and its own closing clause warns only against reading a SECOND export endpoint as a third trigger. **The same sentence in one document justified two exclusions; one was corrected and the other was not** - the shape this package records as a correction applied to one artifact and not its sibling.

⛔⛔ **THE DATA CLAIM IN THE PARAGRAPH BELOW IS WITHDRAWN - IT WAS FALSE, AND IT WAS THE PREMISE THIS ROW'S DEFERRAL RESTED ON.** It read: *"`SL-030`'s authorization decisions already emit audit rows, so the data such an alert would consume accumulates from now."* **They do not.** Measured 2026-08-30 while sizing `WBS-26.2`: **18 write features in `Topics` use `IAuditSink` and ZERO read features do**, and the entire `Abac/` folder - `ConfidentialityRequirement`, `AbacProviders`, `StreamScopeRequirement` - contains no audit emission whatever. `Topics.TopicRestricted` exists but is the event for MARKING a topic restricted, not for accessing one. **So nothing anywhere recorded who read which `Restricted` topic, and this signal was undetectable by ANY mechanism - Seq included - until something recorded it.** ⭐ THE DISTINCTION THAT HID IT: SL-030's ABAC decisions really ARE taken on every read; they are simply not AUDITED, and a decision being taken is invisibly different from a decision being recorded unless you look for an `IAuditSink` in the authorization path. `LL-006`'s family - the row is a proxy for the code, and no identifier or status check could reveal it. ✅ **`DEC-099` d1 ruled that read-auditing IS added**, following `Meetings.RecordingAccessed`'s precedent, and `WBS-26.2` builds it.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED RATHER THAN BUILT, and the reasoning is `DW-087`'s because the situation is the same. Anomaly detection needs a baseline and there is none: any threshold set today would be a guess dressed as a control. ⛔ The sentence that stood here about SL-030's audit rows is WITHDRAWN - see the block above. Alerting also belongs to the ops/runtime group separately blocked on a running stack. ✅ `NFR-065` resolves the threshold problem rather than waiting on it: its second clause requires the BASIS of each threshold to be recorded as either derived from observed usage or PROVISIONAL PENDING A BASELINE, so *provisional* is a legitimate answer and the control can exist while the baseline accumulates (`DEC-099` d3).

⚠ `DOC-067`'s SENTENCE IS NOT EDITED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `docs/` is the frozen read-only archive (`AGENTS.md`, superseded 2026-07-22) and `DEC-091` d3 declined an exception to that freeze. `DEF-118` records the document's staleness generally; this row records this specific consequence. **A reader who finds that sentence and not this row would conclude the gap is intentional and still argued for.** ▸▸ ACTIVATED 2026-08-29 by DEC-094 / SC-038, and scheduled as WBS-26.2 in SL-035. ⚠ THIS WAS AN OVERRIDE: the agent recommended carrying this row Open, and the reasoning-against is preserved in DEC-094 so the activation is not later read as agreement (DEC-071 d3's precedent). ⚠ ACTIVATION DOES NOT CREATE AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION - one written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently (trap 16c), so the criterion is written in the batch that produces the evidence. Built as ONE UNIT with DW-087 - they are two signals of one control, C-INS-01, and splitting them is exactly how one half was corrected and the other was not.

✅✅ **DONE - BUILT AS `WBS-26.2`, PR `#331` → `c273294c`, 2026-08-30.** `Topics.RestrictedTopicAccessed` now records every successful `Restricted` read - the data half that did not exist - and `Topics.RestrictedAccessAnomaly` fires when one principal's accesses reach the configured threshold within the window. `AC-157` `Met` (`AV-235`), `NFR-065` → `Implemented`. ⚠ THE RECORDING SITS AFTER THE VISIBILITY CHECK, deliberately: above that line the refusal is indistinguishable from *no such topic*, so logging there would both record reads that never happened and leak the existence of hidden topics into the audit log. ⚠ `DW-095` records that C-INS-01 names FIVE signals and this pair is two of them.

`C-AUTH-05`'s SoD-4 CLAUSE HAS NO HARD GUARD IN CODE - IT IS THE ONE MEMBER OF A FIVE-PART P1 CONTROL THAT NEVER SHIPPED, AND ITS ONLY RECORD IS A `Partial` IN A FROZEN ARCHIVE THAT ASKED A LATER BATCH TO VERIFY IT. NO LATER BATCH DID.

WHAT THE CATALOGUE SPECIFIES. `docs/domain/security-controls.md` lists `C-AUTH-05` as **Segregation-of-duties guards (SoD-1...SoD-5) enforced as hard authZ checks**, P1, mapped to ASVS `V8`, addressing threats `T-04`, `T-05`, `T-07`, `T-11` and abuse cases `AB-1`, `AB-2`, `AB-3`, `AB-7`. SoD-4 is *"decision recorder != sole owner/presenter + COI exclusion"*.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, MEASURED 2026-08-29. Across `src/**/*.cs` the identifiers `SoD-1`, `SoD-2`, `SoD-3` and `SoD-5` appear 11, 10, 13 and 11 times respectively. **`SoD-4` appears ZERO times.** The four non-zero siblings are the control that proves the sweep had a subject (`LL-013`), so the zero is an absence and not a broken scan. ✅ THIS HALF OF THE ROW STANDS - it was re-measured 2026-08-29 in the `WBS-26.1` interview and is unchanged.

ITS ONLY RECORD IS IN THE FROZEN ARCHIVE AND IT IS A DEFERRAL, NOT A DECISION. `DOC-067` (`docs/validation/security-controls-audit.md`, last touched 2026-07-17) records SoD-4 as **`Partial - no distinct hard guard found; verify in a later batch`**. That sentence is the whole of the project's memory of this gap, it sits in a read-only archive `AGENTS.md` superseded on 2026-07-22, and the later batch it asks for never happened.

⛔⛔ **THE REGISTER-SWEEP CLAIM THAT STOOD HERE IS WITHDRAWN, AND ITS CAUSE IS NOW DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN GUESSED.** This paragraph read: *"A sweep of the deferred-work, defect, open-question, requirement, decision and ADR registers for `SoD-4` or the COI rule returns **ZERO rows**, against a control term `SoD` that is non-zero in five of those six registers. **Nothing in the live package knows this control is unbuilt.**"* **The COI half of that is FALSE.** Re-run 2026-08-29 over the same six registers, the sweep returns **`FR-076`** (a requirement that specifies the COI feature AND specifies its strength), **`DW-004`** (Conflict-of-interest tracking per vote, Phase 2) and **`ADR-0010`** (whose consequences name *conflict-of-interest recusals are expressible*). The SoD-4 half stands; the COI half does not.

⭐⭐ **THE CAUSE IS AN ORTHOGRAPHY MISMATCH AND IT WAS ISOLATED, NOT INFERRED.** This row's own `custom_attributes` recorded the instrument - the pattern `'SoD-4|conflict of interest|COI exclusion'` - so the diagnosis did not need guessing, only reading. **The register spells it `conflict-of-interest` with HYPHENS; the pattern spelled it with SPACES.** Measured with one variable changed and nothing else: `conflict of interest` returns **1** row across those six registers, `conflict-of-interest` returns **7**, and the delta is exactly `FR-076`, `DW-004`, `ADR-0010` and this row's own descendants. ⚠⚠ **THE ONE ROW THE ORIGINAL PATTERN MATCHED WAS THIS ONE** - the sweep found its own query string and nothing else, which is trap 30's *a scanner you write can measure itself* in its purest form.

⚠⚠⚠ **AND THE CONTROL TERM DID NOT SAVE IT, WHICH IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES.** `LL-013`'s discipline was FOLLOWED here: a control term (`SoD`) was run and was non-zero in five of six registers, so the sweep was proven to have a subject. **But the control was a DIFFERENT TOKEN from the one that failed.** `SoD` is spelled the same way everywhere; `conflict-of-interest` is not. A control proves the scan reached the corpus - it cannot prove that THIS pattern matches the corpus's spelling of THIS concept. Filed as `LL-033`, now Approved and pinned.

WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN A DEFECT. The gap is real and measured, but the REQUIRED STRENGTH is genuinely ambiguous and that ambiguity is the reason this needs a human rather than a fix. `C-AUTH-05`'s own text calls SoD-1..SoD-5 *"hard authZ checks"*, and yet within the same sentence SoD-2 is qualified *"warn+audit"* and `DOC-067` records SoD-2 as `Met (soft, per spec)`. So the catalogue already contains one member enforced softly by design. Whether SoD-4 is a hard refusal, a warn-and-audit like SoD-2, or a COI declaration workflow is a specification question nobody has answered, and building the wrong one is worse than the gap: a hard guard on *recorder != owner* could refuse legitimate minute-taking in a committee of twenty where roles overlap by necessity.

⚠ DO NOT READ SoD-3's PRESENCE AS COVERING THIS. SoD-3 is *cast != count != chairman override* on VOTING and is well covered. SoD-4 is about who RECORDS a decision relative to who owns or presents it, and about conflict-of-interest exclusion - a different aggregate, a different moment and a different threat. ⛔ AND DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY EDITING `DOC-067`: the archive is frozen and `DEC-091` d3 declined an exception to that freeze. This row IS the correction. ▸▸ ACTIVATED 2026-08-29 by DEC-094 / SC-038, and scheduled as WBS-26.1 in SL-035. ⚠ THIS WAS AN OVERRIDE: the agent recommended carrying this row Open, and the reasoning-against is preserved in DEC-094 so the activation is not later read as agreement (DEC-071 d3's precedent).

▸▸▸ **THE STRENGTH QUESTION IS ANSWERED - `DEC-095` (2026-08-29), APPLIED BY `SC-039`. DO NOT RE-ASK IT.** **(a) SoD-4's RECORDER CLAUSE IS WARN-AND-AUDIT** (d1), following SoD-2's shipped pattern: recording is allowed, the overlap is flagged, a distinct audit event is emitted. A hard refusal was considered and REJECTED, on `NFR-064`'s own reasoning that it could block legitimate minute-taking. **(b) SoD-4's COI CLAUSE IS COVERED BY `FR-076` AND STAYS PHASE 2** (d2) - which is the ruling the corrected sweep above made possible, and without which `WBS-26.1` would have been built with a COI exclusion that `FR-076`'s own words forbid. **(c) ALL FIVE STRENGTHS ARE RECORDED IN `DEC-095` d4.**

✅✅ **DONE - BUILT AS `WBS-26.1`, PR `#330` → `42e948b8`, 2026-08-30, and the item is `Implemented` by the operator's verdict (`DEC-098` d1).** The guard covers topic owner AND agenda presenter (`DEC-096` d2), warn-and-audit: recording is allowed, `Decision.RecordedByConflictedActor` is persisted, and a distinct `Decisions.DecisionRecordedByConflictedActor` audit ROW is emitted. `AC-156` `Met` (`AV-234`) across ALL FIVE SoD rules; `NFR-064` → `Implemented`. ⚠ The COI half is NOT built and must not be read as missing work here - `FR-076` carries it at Phase 2 with `DW-004`, per (b) above.

title:
SoD-4's CONFLICT FLAG REACHES THE DTO BUT IS NOT RENDERED, WHILE SoD-2's EQUIVALENT IS SURFACED END TO END - THE TWO WARN-AND-AUDIT RULES ARE NOW VISIBLE TO DIFFERENT AUDIENCES.

WHAT SHIPPED IN WBS-26.1. `Decision.RecordedByConflictedActor` is persisted, exposed on `DecisionDetailDto`, and emitted as a distinct `Decisions.DecisionRecordedByConflictedActor` audit event asserted as a ROW. So the signal is durable, filterable in the audit log, and available to any client that reads the decision.

WHAT DID NOT. It is not rendered anywhere in the SPA. Measured 2026-08-29, SoD-2's counterpart IS: `ApprovedBySoleAuthor` runs from `MinutesDtos.cs` through `src/api/minutes.ts` into `MeetingMinutes.tsx`, with a component test and an e2e spec (`p17b-sole-author.spec.ts`). Two rules recorded at the SAME strength are therefore surfaced differently - one to a reviewer reading the screen, one only to a reviewer reading the audit log.

WHY IT WAS NOT BUILT IN THAT ITEM, stated so this does not read as an oversight. `NFR-064`'s verification detail names, for a warn-and-audit rule, *the warning AND the resulting AuditEvent as a ROW* - it does not name a user interface, and `DEC-095` d1's ruling is about ENFORCEMENT STRENGTH rather than presentation. `WBS-26.1` was already an `L` carrying a persisted field, a migration, a widened cross-module contract and a new one; adding a screen would have expanded it past what either decision asked for. ⚠ AND IT IS NOT A FREE ADDITION: any new surface is bound by `INV-014`, so it needs its own `.dc.html` reference or must be flagged explicitly as a no-reference composition.

WHAT WOULD MOVE THIS ROW. Either a stated ask for the flag to be visible on the decision detail screen, or the next piece of work that touches that screen for another reason - at which point adding a badge beside the existing attribution is small, and doing it THEN avoids paying the design-fidelity cost twice. ⚠ Check the Decisions `.dc.html` in `ACMP product context/` first: if it draws no such badge, this is a no-reference composition and must say so.

⚠ DO NOT READ THIS AS THE RULE BEING HALF-BUILT. The control is complete and evidenced at the strength the operator set. This row is about PARITY OF PRESENTATION between two rules, which is a product question rather than a security one.

C-INS-01 NAMES FIVE ANOMALY SIGNALS AND `WBS-26.2` BUILT TWO - THE OTHER THREE WERE NEVER DECLINED, NEVER SCHEDULED, AND UNTIL NOW NEVER RECORDED.

WHAT THE CONTROL SPECIFIES. `C-INS-01` reads: *"Anomaly alerting via Seq (the detection tripwire for privileged insiders P3): alert rules on **bulk/atypical export volume**, **atypical access to `Restricted` topics or recordings**, **role grants/delegations**, **bursts of authz denials**, and **off-hours privileged actions**."* Five signals, one P1 control, mapped to `T-04`, `T-05`, `T-07`, `T-10` and abuse cases `AB-1`, `AB-2`, `AB-5`, `AB-6`.

WHAT IS BUILT. `WBS-26.2` (`c273294c`) delivers the FIRST TWO: `Audit.BulkExportAnomaly` on export volume, and `Topics.RestrictedTopicAccessed` plus `Topics.RestrictedAccessAnomaly` on Restricted-topic access. `AC-157` records them with a `Met` verdict and names this gap in its own exclusions.

⚠⚠ WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AT ALL, AND IT IS THE ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS. `DOC-067` deliberately declined TWO signals in writing, each with a stated reason, and those two became `DW-087` and `DW-092` when their premises turned false. **The other three were never declined - they were never mentioned.** A signal nobody argued against leaves no trace, so the register recorded a two-signal control where the catalogue specifies five, and `WBS-26.2` closing would have read as C-INS-01 being satisfied. That is the shape this project keeps finding: an absence produces no output to be suspicious of.

WHAT EACH REMAINING SIGNAL WOULD NEED, sized only enough to say it is not free. **Role grants/delegations** - `C-AUDIT-05` already requires these to *emit high-importance audit events feeding `C-INS-01`*, so the DATA most likely exists and the work is a detection rule; verify before assuming. **Bursts of authz denials** - `AuthorizationBehavior` and `AuditingAuthorizationResultHandler` already audit refusals (`RefusalAuditTests` asserts the rows), so again the data plausibly exists. **Off-hours privileged actions** - needs a definition of *off-hours* before it can be detected at all, which is a committee question rather than an engineering one, and probably an `OQ-` before a build.

⚠ THE ATYPICAL-**RECORDINGS** HALF IS ALSO NOT BUILT, and it is nearer than the three above: `C-INS-01` says *"Restricted topics **or recordings**"*, and `Meetings.RecordingAccessed` already records successful recording access. Only the detection rule is missing, and `AnomalyDetector` is now the obvious home for it.

⚠ DO NOT READ THIS AS `WBS-26.2` BEING INCOMPLETE. That item built exactly what `DEC-094` d3 activated - the two signals `DOC-067` had declined - and `NFR-065` was written for those two. This row is the DIFFERENCE between that requirement and the control, which nothing else in the register states.
activation_trigger: Any of: (a) a decision to complete C-INS-01 rather than the two signals NFR-065 covers - at which point each remaining signal needs the same treatment WBS-26.2 gave these two, including a threshold basis recorded as derived or provisional; (b) the ASVS L2 assessment NFR-018 awaits raising the gap, since C-INS-01 is mapped to V8 and V16 and DOC-070's evidence pack cites the control; (c) the running-stack work reaching Seq alert configuration, where the absence of three of five rules becomes visible to whoever writes them; or (d) an off-hours definition being settled by the committee, which unblocks that signal specifically and is the only one of the three blocked on a human answer rather than on engineering.
